## Purpose and entry points
Herdr is a Rust terminal-native multiplexer for coding agents: it manages real PTY-backed panes, tracks agent state, persists detachable sessions, and exposes a socket API for automation. The executable starts in `src/main.rs`, parses commands in `src/cli.rs`, and routes interactive client/server runtime modes through `src/client/mod.rs` and `src/server/mod.rs`.

## Runtime topology
A local server owns session state, terminals, PTYs, persistence, and API subscriptions; one or more clients attach to render and control that state. Server discovery/connection uses socket paths and client transport, while headless operation supports remote or noninteractive control. Core boundaries: `src/server/socket_paths.rs`, `src/server/client_transport.rs`, `src/server/headless.rs`.

## Application state and workspace model
The app layer coordinates mutable session state: workspaces contain tabs, layouts, panes, terminal targets, and worktrees. Actions from UI, CLI, API, or server events converge here rather than directly mutating terminal processes. Key orchestration paths are `src/app/state.rs`, `src/app/actions.rs`, and `src/app/session.rs`; workspace/Git aggregation lives in `src/workspace.rs`, `src/workspace/aggregate.rs`, and `src/workspace/git/mod.rs`.

## Terminal and PTY pipeline
Pane creation attaches a shell or agent process to a PTY actor. Terminal output is interpreted into terminal state, pane metadata, title/state changes, graphics, and agent-detection signals; input travels in the reverse direction through key/mouse encoding to the PTY. Primary components: `src/pty/actor.rs`, `src/pane/terminal.rs`, `src/terminal/runtime.rs`. The project vendors or binds Ghostty terminal functionality through `src/ghostty/mod.rs` and `src/ghostty/bindings.rs`.

## Interactive client and rendering
The interactive client collects raw terminal input, applies configured keybindings and UI navigation, then renders panes, tabs, sidebars, overlays, and status into the host terminal. This is a terminal UI, not a web application. Important paths: `src/client/input.rs`, `src/app/input/mod.rs`, `src/ui.rs`; visual terminal protocols include `src/kitty_graphics.rs` and `src/protocol/render_ansi.rs`.

## Agent lifecycle, detection, and integrations
Herdr identifies supported agents from terminal behavior/manifests, presents their working/blocked/done state, and installs or executes integration hooks that report state. Detection definitions are data-driven TOML manifests; integrations contain agent-specific assets and configuration edits. Boundaries: `src/pane/agent_detection.rs`, `src/detect/manifest.rs`, `src/integration/registry.rs`. Agent resume/handoff logic is separated in `src/agent_resume.rs` and `src/handoff_runtime.rs`.

## Automation API and plugins
A versioned socket API offers control over agents, sessions, panes, tabs, workspaces, worktrees, integrations, and plugins. API schemas define the external contract; event hubs/subscriptions support asynchronous observation and waiting. Relevant paths: `src/api/server.rs`, `src/api/schema.rs`, `src/api/event_hub.rs`. Plugins execute through app-side plugin runtime/context boundaries in `src/app/api/plugins/runtime.rs` and `src/app/api/plugins/context.rs`; a separate Cloudflare Worker backs the marketplace at `workers/plugin-marketplace/src/index.ts`.

## Durability and platforms
Session snapshots, restoration, and plugin registry persistence allow detach/reattach and restart recovery. Platform adapters isolate Linux, macOS, and Windows behavior, including PTY differences. Paths: `src/persist/snapshot.rs`, `src/persist/restore.rs`, `src/platform/mod.rs`. The main runtime is one Rust binary; build/release support includes Cargo, Nix (`flake.nix`), and GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/release.yml`).
